title: Command S on a video edit does what the user picks
goal: Once a video edit can be saved as a project, Command S has to mean one thing on it. The user picks whether it always saves the project, or writes a plain trim of one recording back over that recording as the old recording window did, and this task builds that answer.
notes: Replaces the withdrawn card on trim-becomes-a-tool-and-the-recording-window-ret (2026-09-20), which asked about one trimmed recording with an arrow on it. Depends on a-video-edit-can-be-saved-as-a-project-and-opene for the project format. Code: EditorState.saveDocument / saveAffordance / SaveAffordance.forDocument (PhotonzCore). The old recording window's write-back path lives in the recording window code that trim-becomes-a-tool retires; option b reuses it for the one-untouched-clip case.
acceptance: Command S on an edited video does what the answered card says, at Next defaults, with no switch changed
The File menu, the edited dot and the close sheet agree with it (SaveAffordance stays the one answer they all read)
A walk presses Command S on a cut, multi-clip edit and on a plain trim of one recording, and checks what landed on disk
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
